app.title: DepremNabız AI — Seismic catalogue analytics, exposure screening and Sentinel-1 pair planning
app.summary: A person picks an earthquake catalogue source: bundled demo data, a live query of the public USGS catalogue with a lookback and minimum magnitude, or an uploaded CSV or Excel file that is normalised to a common event schema. A headline row then shows the event count, the maximum magnitude, the median depth, the share of shallow events and a Gutenberg–Richter b-value. Tabs show the events on a map with exploratory DBSCAN clusters, daily counts, magnitude through time, the magnitude distribution, magnitude against depth, a rolling event-rate anomaly screen, and a data-quality table. Two more tabs count user-supplied exposure points within a chosen radius of the largest events, and search Sentinel-1 acquisitions to plan same-orbit image pairs and summarise uploaded displacement points. The cleaned catalogue can be downloaded as a CSV.

task.text: Load an event catalogue for a region, summarise its magnitudes, depths and rates, flag unusual daily activity, and screen the largest events against nearby exposure points and satellite acquisitions.

data.text: A catalogue of timestamped events with coordinates, depth and magnitude. Alongside it come a table of exposure points with optional categories and weights, a catalogue of satellite acquisitions with orbit metadata, and optional processed displacement points.
data.item: one earthquake event with time, latitude, longitude, depth and magnitude

stage.text: exploring and summarising a freshly retrieved event catalogue, before detailed hazard or deformation studies

mechanism.text: A sidebar sets the source and filters, and every view on the page is recomputed from the resulting cleaned catalogue: headline statistics, then tabbed maps and charts. The exposure and satellite tabs each take their own upload or search, combined with the catalogue or the acquisition list, and show the results as tables and maps.

field.text: earthquake-catalogue statistics with InSAR acquisition planning in seismology

workflow.name: summarize an event catalogue and screen it against nearby points of interest

steps.here: A radio chooses demo data, live USGS or an uploaded CSV or Excel file. Sliders set the lookback in days and a minimum magnitude, and uploads are normalised and cleaned into a common event schema.
The Data quality tab lists missing values, duplicates, invalid coordinates and timestamp coverage for the loaded catalogue.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Events go on a map sized and coloured by magnitude, with hover showing DBSCAN cluster labels, next to daily-count bars, magnitude through time, a magnitude histogram and a magnitude–depth scatter with depth reversed.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Headline metrics give the count, maximum magnitude, median depth and share of events at 20 km or shallower. A b-value is estimated above a completeness magnitude taken from the minimum-magnitude slider, and daily counts are z-scored against a 14-day rolling baseline, with anomalies marked by crosses.

steps.step: count nearby points within a radius
steps.here: Exposure points are uploaded (or demo points used), a radius slider sets the screening distance, and the largest events are listed with nearby point counts and summed weights, sorted by weight, beside a map of the points.

A Sentinel-1 catalogue is loaded from the demo or searched live over a date range, same-orbit pairs within a maximum gap are listed, and an optional upload of processed displacement points gives summary statistics and a diverging-colour map.
A button downloads the filtered, cleaned catalogue as a CSV.

distinctive: The b-value uses a completeness magnitude tied to the minimum-magnitude filter, and is withheld when fewer than 20 events lie above it.
Rate anomalies are rolling z-scores of daily counts, framed explicitly as statistical deviations and not forecasts.
Exposure is a proximity proxy: weighted point counts within a radius of the largest events, not damage or loss.
Satellite acquisitions are grouped by relative orbit and orbit direction and paired chronologically for downstream interferometry, rather than processed in the app.
Every view is labelled with the active data source and the latest record time, so demo and live data are never confused.
